title: Degree-diameter problem (4,3): a large graph of maximum degree 4 and diameter 3
statement: Find a graph with maximum degree at most 4 and diameter at most 3, with as many vertices n as possible; it shows N(4,3) >= n. The largest known such graph, by Allwright (1992), has 41 vertices; a graph with more vertices improves it.
submission: Text file: one graph in graph6 or sparse6 (as House of Graphs gives them; an optional >>graph6<< or >>sparse6<< header is allowed), or an edge list, one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0.
score: n, the number of vertices of a graph with maximum degree at most 4 and diameter at most 3 (larger is better)

best_known.source: N(4,3) >= 41: Allwright (1992), in F. Comellas's table of the largest known graphs for the degree-diameter problem (last changed 2 Nov 2026), as mirrored by Leaps in Bounds at commit 4521e13; read 8 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: F. Comellas, The (Degree, Diameter) Problem for Graphs
